visuals.heading: Key Ideas at a Glance

items.text: Both lead to real consulting work; they differ in cost, timeline, starting pay, and how fast you reach strategy-heavy client work.
There is no single correct door into consulting.
The dominant path into MBB and most tier-2 strategy roles in India runs through a small set of top B-schools, where firms run structured campus processes each placement season.
Big 4 firms and many boutique consultancies hire directly from undergraduate campuses, off-campus applications, and lateral moves from adjacent roles like business analysis, operations, or finance.

blocks.heading: Case Interviews Exist Because They Compress

items.text: Consulting interviews and consulting work both run on the same test: can you break an ambiguous business problem into a clean structure, form a hypothesis early, and use data to prove or kill it, instead of researching endlessly before forming a view.
Mental math, market sizing, and reading a P&L without a calculator in front of a partner is a baseline skill, not a bonus one.

blocks.heading: Mistakes That Sink Otherwise Strong Candidates

items.text: Candidates who land MBB and tier-2 offers typically start structured preparation 6 to 9 months ahead of campus season.

Taking the offer without an honest look at your own tolerance for 55-65 hour weeks and 2-4 travel nights most weeks, sometimes stretching to 70-80 hours in deliverable weeks, is one of the most common regret patterns among first-year consultants.

If you are still early, decide which door realistically fits your timeline and budget: the MBA route if you can commit the time and cost for a shot at MBB and tier-2 strategy firms, or the direct-entry route into Big 4 and boutique firms if you want to start sooner or want to test the fit before committing to further study.

If you are unsure whether consulting genuinely fits how you like to work, or whether the MBA route is worth the cost for your situation, the career resources library and Career & Skills Compass can help you compare it against other high-exposure career paths before you commit real prep time to it.

If you are choosing between the MBA route, direct entry, or a completely different path, or trying to work out whether your background and goals actually fit consulting's pace, a session with career guidance can help you work through the decision with real numbers instead of guesswork, so you back the route that genuinely unlocks high-income opportunities for your profile instead of chasing a brand name.

visuals.heading: This Is Not Independent Consulting

items.text: You are an employee of a firm with a fixed salary, benefits, and a defined promotion ladder.
The firm finds the clients, staffs you on projects, and sets the engagement scope.
Work is done in structured teams under an engagement manager or partner.
Income is predictable month to month; risk sits with the firm, not you.

blocks.heading: How to Prepare Beyond Case-Practice Reps

items.text: Complete 30-50 full verbal practice cases with real partners, not solo reading.
Rebuild your resume around outcomes and numbers, not just responsibilities.
Reach out to alumni or current consultants for short, specific informational calls.
Apply off-campus in parallel if your campus process is narrow or non-existent.

blocks.heading: What Actually Happens in the Interview Process

items.text: Resume and cover-letter screen.
An aptitude or written test at some firms.
Two to four case interview rounds.
A final partner or leadership round.
